prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: FULL LANDSCAPE GAMEPLAY SCENE CONCEPT for a 2D gently top-down prison escape game, for USER REVIEW ONLY.
Reference is the current gameplay screenshot. Keep the established warm grey-green stone tiles, pale warm stone coping, worn grey-green iron, inked hand-painted comic look, compact orange-clad characters, dark navy guard, merchant, police dog, and same overall cream-paper HUD layout. Remove the Windows title bar. A polished wide horizontal 16:10 game screen, map fills the frame beneath/behind HUD. Fixed gently elevated ORTHOGRAPHIC view, horizontal and vertical map axes, no diamond isometric perspective or converging vanishing points. Preserve screenshot's LOCAL COMPOSITION: solitary rooms at left, long vertical corridor through center, cafeteria at right; selected spiky-haired orange prisoner near the central corridor just outside left cell, merchant and small laundry cart above him, guard and shepherd lower in central corridor.
PRIMARY AND ABSOLUTE PRIORITY: REDESIGN THE DOORS AS PART OF THE MASONRY BUILDING. Do NOT preserve the reference's oversized standalone bolted iron rectangles. Current reference gate failures are exactly what needs correcting.
Architecture specification:
- Warm pale stone walls have one coherent physical thickness, front shaded face and matching top coping. Room walls, door jambs, and openings connect as continuous construction.
- Redesign a coherent CUTAWAY BUILDING, not simply a smaller gate pasted onto the old 18-unit low wall. The visible door height should be approximately 1.4 to 1.7 times the 60-unit orange character height, about90 to100 units, NEVER the current 160 to180 units. Adjacent masonry jambs, wall-end column heads, wall faces and top coping rise and join at that SAME architectural level. Metal frame recessed below/inside the masonry lintel/cut top, never sticking up as a separate tall arch. Reduce/remove selected foreground wall sections to reveal the room interior, while keeping continuous joined returns and shared construction at each doorway. Cutaway transitions must be intentional and architectural, with coherent pillar heads and top surfaces. Do NOT only scale down a freestanding metal rectangle and leave unrelated thin low wall behind it.
- Door jambs are built INTO masonry, held between stone block reveals. Only a narrow recessed steel edge visible inside the stone opening. No independent fat steel posts, no giant iron arch, no floating door frame or separate prop standing on a low wall.
- Stone coping terminates and returns neatly around the door reveals. Metal framing shares the wall's thickness/camera view. No stone wall passing across a door leaf or open passage.
- Floor-level thin worn threshold aligned with room tile direction, no raised platform or thick foundation.
- Front walls lower/cut away for room visibility; modest short side/reveal faces show real wall thickness, no extra decorative tower piers.
LEFT SOLITARY CELL: keep the visible simple narrow cot, toilet/sink and vent. Put a CLOSED SOLID grey-green metal solitary door into the cell's SOUTH/front horizontal wall near its right half, near the location of the current solid door. Door occupies a real gap in stone wall, a recessed steel slab seen at the SAME architectural cutaway height as adjacent masonry, small shut inspection hatch and brass latch, no bars. It is part of the cell front wall, not a full-height standalone rectangle. Match character-relative scale.
RIGHT CAFETERIA ENTRANCE: put an OPEN BARRED gate into the cafeteria's NORTH/front horizontal stone boundary at roughly the existing entrance location. Show a clear readable floor-level walk-through opening and continuous corridor tile leading inside. Barred sliding leaf parked/recessed into an adjacent LEFT wall pocket, tucked beneath the cut coping; no full-height independent open frame. This opening is the same physical scale and construction as the solitary doorway. Small access controller attached to the adjacent masonry reveal, no glow. Include simple plain cafeteria table/benches inside to explain the passage.
HUD: preserve current screenshot's arrangement and restrained design: upper-left cream time card '13:50 吃饭休息' and simple day timeline, adjacent '日常表'; three small cream partner cards stacked on left with orange portraits, short Chinese skill/state text and teal/ochre meters; top-right escaped counter '逃脱 0/3', coins '0', pause button; below that a compact minimap; bottom-left translucent directional joystick; bottom-right small backpack/skill controls. Do not add new complicated UI, callout boxes, insets, legends, bright arrows or extra interaction halos. Existing selected-character teal ring can remain subtle. Chinese typography clear and similar to reference, don't turn this into a poster.
Composition reads as ONE actual gameplay camera screenshot, not separate asset sprites or a closeup board. Main payoff is seeing a CLOSED SOLID left cell door and an OPEN BARRED right cafeteria opening neatly integrated with their stone walls at the real game viewing scale. Quiet worn materials, subtle soft ground contact shadows, readable characters. Avoid huge gates, floating elements, exaggerated perspective, dramatic lighting, neon, horror, modern glossy metal, door geometry disconnected from wall, opaque fill in open doorway, or wall crossing door slab.
